original_post_text:
Thanks to the DFW poker community for keeping me plugged in as this develops. 

Lodge Card Club Update — This Just Got Much More Serious

We now have answers on why TABC raided The Lodge Card Club in Round Rock this past Tuesday — and it’s bigger than anyone initially assumed.

According to a statement from TABC Director of Communications Chris Porter, the agency’s Financial Crimes Unit, along with its Special Investigations Unit and Operations Bureau, executed a search and seizure warrant as part of an ongoing investigation into suspected money laundering and illegal gambling. 

Early speculation centered around liquor licensing issues or underage drinking, which makes sense given TABC’s name. Those assumptions appear to have been incorrect. 

Approximately 20 TABC agents were involved in the operation, along with officers from the Williamson County Sheriff’s Office and the IRS.  The IRS being involved is significant, this is now a federal level matter.

No arrests have been made and no charges have been filed against the business at this time.  The investigation remains ongoing.

The Lodge remains closed with no reopening timetable announced.

We will continue to follow this story closely.

#TheLodge #PokerNews #GameIntegrity #TexasPoker

expanded_body:
Originally posted March 12, 2026.

Thanks to the DFW poker community for keeping me plugged in as this develops.

We now have answers on why TABC raided The Lodge Card Club in Round Rock on Tuesday, March 10 — and it's bigger than anyone initially assumed.

According to a statement from TABC Director of Communications Chris Porter to PokerNews (https://www.pokernews.com/news/2026/03/lodge-card-club-money-laundering-charges-50804.htm), the agency's Financial Crimes Unit, along with its Special Investigations Unit and Operations Bureau, executed a search and seizure warrant as part of an ongoing investigation into suspected money laundering and illegal gambling.

Early speculation centered around liquor licensing issues or underage drinking, which makes sense given TABC's name. Those assumptions appear to have been incorrect.

Approximately 20 TABC agents were involved in the operation, along with officers from the Williamson County Sheriff's Office and the IRS. The IRS being involved is significant — this is a federal-level matter.

No arrests have been made and no charges have been filed against the business at this time. The investigation remains ongoing, and The Lodge remains closed with no reopening timetable announced.

We will continue to follow this story closely.

— Sham
